rationale: The buyer is a nameable B2B role — ops leads, procurement managers, and SaaS founders at 5–200 person companies who depend on third-party tools and face real financial risk when a vendor dies. Willingness to pay is plausible given the business cost of vendor failure (emergency migrations, data loss, lost SLA), but there is no direct 'I'd pay $X/mo for this' signal yet — only HN resonance. The service can mostly run autonomously (automated monitoring + alerting), but building a reliable vendor-health signal layer (scraping SaaSHub, integrating multiple mortality signals) requires meaningful upfront integration work, keeping both buildability and operational autonomy in the mid-range. Validate before committing to build: run a short outreach to ops/procurement leads to confirm they'd pay rather than build this internally.
solution_plan: WHAT: A vendor-health monitoring micro-service that watches the SaaS tools a company uses and sends a weekly alert when any show mortality signals (shrinking reviews, no changelog updates, low HN/Reddit activity, SaaSHub 'dead' flags). BUILD: The factory sets up a Claude-driven data-gathering pipeline pulling from SaaSHub, G2, and public changelogs; a simple intake form where a buyer pastes their tool stack; and a Stripe subscription link — no coding by you. SELL: The factory identifies ops leads and SaaS founders on LinkedIn and Product Hunt, drafts personalised outreach emails explaining the vendor-risk angle, and queues them for your one-click approval before sending. MAINTAIN: Weekly monitoring runs on a schedule; Claude composes and sends the alert digest to each subscriber; Stripe handles billing; you only approve outreach batches and occasional edge-case alerts the system flags for human review. CAVEAT: Data reliability is the key risk — if public mortality signals are too noisy, the service will produce false alarms that erode trust fast; a small paid-pilot with 3–5 companies before full build is strongly recommended.
notes: No build_gate failures — operational_autonomy (7), buildability_with_ai (6), buyer_clarity (7), willingness_to_pay (5) all at or above their floors. Stage is validate because total (5.8) does not yet reach min_total_to_build (6.5). Main gap: zero responsiveness signal and no explicit price/budget evidence. A 10-reply outreach sprint to ops leads would resolve both.
